full_judgment: 12. We have also noticed in the preamble and in section 3 of the new Act that the Act covers not only the offence of corruption but also certain other offences. The other offences are mentioned in the schedule. From the schedule we find that besides the offences under the Act, offences under Act II of 1947, certain offences of the Penal Code, offences under the Control of Essential Commodities Act, 1956, the Hoarding and Black Market Act 1956, the Prevention of Smuggling Act. 1952, the Essential Articles (Price Control and Anti-Hoarding) Act 1953, the Imports (Control) Act, 1950, the East Bengal (Smuggling of Food grains) Act 1950 are also included. Under section 3, regarding an offence under any of these Acts, the Bureau may inquire and investigate. The offenders under most of these Acts are not public servants nor connected with public servants for example, a trader, hoarder, importer, dealer, smuggler are not public servants. They will be punishable under the respective Act even if they have no collusion with any public servant. In other words, without any collusion with any public servant offences under the above Act may be committed and in that case the individual offender may be tried and punished under the Act of 1957. So, we find that any private person whether he has any connection with a public servant or not can also be tried and punished under the Act of 1957.
